name: hashid
summary: Software to identify the different types of hashes used to encrypt data.
highlights: -e — list all possible hash algorithms including salted passwords
-m — show corresponding Hashcat mode in output
-j — show corresponding JohnTheRipper format in output

flags.name: --extended
flags.description: list all possible hash algorithms including salted passwords

flags.name: --mode
flags.description: show corresponding Hashcat mode in output

flags.name: --john
flags.description: show corresponding JohnTheRipper format in output

flags.name: --help
flags.description: show this help message and exit

flags.name: --version
flags.description: show program's version number and exit

examples.explanation: Identify hashes from `stdin` (through typing, copying and pasting, or piping the hash into the program)
Identify hashes on a file (one hash per line)
Show all possible hash types (including salted hashes)
Show `hashcat`'s mode number and `john`'s format string of the hash types
Save output to a file instead of printing to `stdout`
